commands.name: caveman
commands.description: Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept. Use for /caveman, "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "be brief", "less tokens". Stays on until "stop caveman" or "normal mode". (user)

commands.name: handoff
commands.description: Write a handoff document another agent can resume this work from — what the task is, what is done, what is left, and how to verify it. Use on a HARNESS CHECKPOINT, or when asked to hand off, checkpoint or pause work for another agent or host. (user)

commands.name: harness
commands.description: Operate the Harness agent fleet for this project — `/harness <idea>` takes an idea to a running fleet in one conversation (install, init, grill into a PRD, start); first-time SETUP (init, seed labels, start) and day-to-day operate (pause/resume/update/status, watch sessions, unstick the GitHub-issue board). Trigger on /harness or requests like "set up the fleet", "start the fleet", "pause the agents", "what's the harness doing". (user)

commands.name: harness-arc
commands.description: Deploy a large multi-plan design to a Harness fleet as a sequenced chain of PRDs that runs unattended to completion, with a wayfinder map holding the decisions the fleet cannot make; `harness supervise` catches the fleet's silent stall modes. Use when a spec or design is too big for one PRD, when the user wants a fleet to run "fully automatic until shipped", when deploying an implementation plan of several plans/stages, or when asked to watch, babysit, or unstick a running Harness fleet. (user)

commands.name: harness-init
commands.description: First-time Harness setup — run the wizard that writes .harness/config and seeds GitHub labels. Trigger on /harness-init or "set up the harness config". (user)

commands.name: harness-issue
commands.description: Inject a discrete implementation issue (or a few) into a LIVE Harness fleet — grill the requirement, confirm a crystallized brief, then launch the headless injector. Trigger on /harness-issue or "add a task to the running fleet". (user)

commands.name: harness-one
commands.description: Work ONE issue by hand while the Harness fleet is paused or usage-HELD — check the precondition, show the issue's cost forecast against live usage and an APPROVE/DENY recommendation, let the human decide, then work the approved issue in this session with a budget re-check before each phase. Trigger on /harness-one or "work one issue while the fleet is paused". (user)

commands.name: harness-pause
commands.description: Pause the Harness fleet — drain (stop claiming new work) or checkpoint each agent to GitHub. Trigger on /harness-pause or "pause the agents". (user)

commands.name: harness-plan
commands.description: Inject a structural plan change into a LIVE Harness fleet — edit PLAN.md and cascade it into the PRD and delta issues. Grill the change, confirm a crystallized brief, then launch the headless injector. Trigger on /harness-plan or "change the plan". (user)

commands.name: harness-prd
commands.description: Extend a LIVE Harness fleet's PRD scope and create the delta issues — grill the new scope, confirm a crystallized brief, then launch the headless injector. Trigger on /harness-prd or "grow the PRD scope". (user)

commands.name: harness-resume
commands.description: Resume a paused Harness fleet — clears the pause and continues here or via crash-recovery sweep. Trigger on /harness-resume or "resume the agents". (user)

commands.name: harness-start
commands.description: Launch the Harness worker pool for this project. Trigger on /harness-start or "start the fleet". (user)

commands.name: harness-status
commands.description: Show the Harness fleet dashboard — the workers and the issue each is running, what's complete vs stuck, complete vs stuck. Trigger on /harness-status or "what's the harness doing". (user)

commands.name: harness-stop
commands.description: Stop the Harness worker pool. Trigger on /harness-stop or "stop the fleet". (user)

commands.name: harness-uninstall
commands.description: Tear down a Harness install/project — remove the shared engine, this project's .harness/, and the /harness skills. Trigger on /harness-uninstall or "uninstall harness", "remove the harness install". (user)

commands.name: subagent-task-tree
commands.description: Execute a multi-task implementation plan as a chained subagent tree — you are the parent controller; you spawn one manager per task; each manager spawns a planner, a plan-auditor, one implementer per subtask, per-subtask auditors, and a final drift-auditor. Use when the user wants to "implement each task using subagents", asks for chained/nested subagents, a manager-per-task build, or subagent-driven execution of a plan/spec with audit gates at every level. (user)

commands.name: to-issues
commands.description: Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable issues on the project issue tracker using tracer-bullet vertical slices. Use when user wants to convert a plan into issues, create implementation tickets, or break down work into issues. (user)

commands.name: to-prd
commands.description: Turn the current conversation context into a PRD and publish it to the project issue tracker. Use when user wants to create a PRD from the current context. (user)

commands.name: writing-plans
commands.description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read FIRST, before you answer, run a command or open a file (already started? read it now); don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file; if nothing hits, load this skill).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring

import csv
import io
import json
import re
import sys
import unicodedata
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_DOWN, getcontext

from .errors import TabulaError, UsageError

PROG = "tabula"
FORMATS = ("text", "csv", "json")
getcontext().prec = 60

NUMBER = re.compile(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)")


# --- numbers -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def to_decimal(text):
    """The Decimal a cell holds, or None when it is not a plain decimal number (no exponent, no thousands marks)."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not NUMBER.fullmatch(text):
        return None
    try:
        return Decimal(text)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def fmt_decimal(number):
    """A Decimal as plain text: no exponent, no negative zero."""
    text = format(number, "f")
    if text.startswith("-") and not text.strip("-0."):
        text = text[1:]
    return text


def _need_number(value):
    number = to_decimal(value)
    if number is None:
        raise TabulaError("%r is not a number" % value)
    return number


def _need_count(arg, name):
    if arg is None or not arg.isdigit():
        raise TabulaError("%s needs a whole number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
    return int(arg)


def _need_decimal_arg(arg, name):
    number = None if arg is None else to_decimal(arg)
    if number is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s needs a number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
    return number


def _no_arg(name, arg):
    if arg is not None:
        raise TabulaError("%s takes no argument, got %r" % (name, arg))


def _need_text(arg, name):
    if arg is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s needs an argument" % name)
    return arg


# --- the table -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Table:
    """Column names and rows of strings. `source` names where it came from, for messages."""

    def __init__(self, columns, rows, source="<table>"):
        self.columns = list(columns)
        self.rows = [list(r) for r in rows]
        self.source = source

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.rows)

    def index(self, name):
        """Position of a column; TabulaError when there is none."""
        try:
            return self.columns.index(name)
        except ValueError:
            raise TabulaError("%s: no column %r (columns: %s)" % (self.source, name, ", ".join(self.columns)))

    def column(self, name):
        at = self.index(name)
        return [row[at] for row in self.rows]

    def dicts(self):
        return [dict(zip(self.columns, row)) for row in self.rows]

    def with_rows(self, rows, columns=None):
        return Table(self.columns if columns is None else columns, rows, self.source)


def parse_text(text, source):
    """CSV text into a Table. Blank lines are ignored; every row must have as many fields as the header."""
    if text.startswith("﻿"):
        text = text[1:]
    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""))
    columns, rows = None, []
    try:
        for fields in reader:
            if not fields:
                continue
            if columns is None:
                for name in fields:
                    if not name.strip():
                        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: empty column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
                if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
                    raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: duplicate column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
                columns = fields
                continue
            if len(fields) != len(columns):
                raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: expected %d fields, found %d"
                                  % (source, reader.line_num, len(columns), len(fields)))
            rows.append(fields)
    except csv.Error as exc:
        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: %s" % (source, reader.line_num, exc))
    if columns is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s: no header line" % source)
    return Table(columns, rows, source)


def load(path):
    """Read a CSV file (UTF-8, optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) into a Table."""
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            raw = fh.read()
    except OSError as exc:
        raise TabulaError("%s: cannot read: %s" % (path, exc.strerror or exc))
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        raise TabulaError("%s: not valid UTF-8" % path)
    return parse_text(text, path)


# --- output --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def render_text(table):
    cells = [table.columns] + table.rows
    widths = [max(len(row[i]) for row in cells) for i in range(len(table.columns))]
    lines = ["  ".join(cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(row, widths)).rstrip() for row in cells]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def render_csv(table):
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(table.columns)
    writer.writerows(table.rows)
    return out.getvalue()


def render_json(table):
    return json.dumps(table.dicts(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"


RENDERERS = {"text": render_text, "csv": render_csv, "json": render_json}


def render(table, fmt="text"):
    return RENDERERS[fmt](table)

1	"""tabula.engine -- the table model, the transforms, the output formats and the command line.
2	
3	This is the one module every command lives in. A command is a function `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` that gets the
4	positional arguments (a list of strings) and the options (a dict) and returns a Table, which `main` then prints in the
5	format asked for (`--format text|csv|json`, text by default). A mistake in a file or in a request raises TabulaError
6	(exit status 1); a command line that is not shaped right raises UsageError (exit status 2).
7	"""
8	import csv
9	import io
10	import json
11	import re
12	import sys
13	import unicodedata
14	from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_DOWN, getcontext
15	
16	from .errors import TabulaError, UsageError
17	
18	PROG = "tabula"
19	FORMATS = ("text", "csv", "json")
20	getcontext().prec = 60
21	
22	NUMBER = re.compile(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)")
23	
24	
25	# --- numbers -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
26	
27	def to_decimal(text):
28	    """The Decimal a cell holds, or None when it is not a plain decimal number (no exponent, no thousands marks)."""
29	    text = text.strip()
30	    if not NUMBER.fullmatch(text):
31	        return None
32	    try:
33	        return Decimal(text)
34	    except InvalidOperation:
35	        return None
36	
37	
38	def fmt_decimal(number):
39	    """A Decimal as plain text: no exponent, no negative zero."""
40	    text = format(number, "f")
41	    if text.startswith("-") and not text.strip("-0."):
42	        text = text[1:]
43	    return text
44	
45	
46	def _need_number(value):
47	    number = to_decimal(value)
48	    if number is None:
49	        raise TabulaError("%r is not a number" % value)
50	    return number
51	
52	
53	def _need_count(arg, name):
54	    if arg is None or not arg.isdigit():
55	        raise TabulaError("%s needs a whole number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
56	    return int(arg)
57	
58	
59	def _need_decimal_arg(arg, name):
60	    number = None if arg is None else to_decimal(arg)
61	    if number is None:
62	        raise TabulaError("%s needs a number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
63	    return number
64	
65	
66	def _no_arg(name, arg):
67	    if arg is not None:
68	        raise TabulaError("%s takes no argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
69	
70	
71	def _need_text(arg, name):
72	    if arg is None:
73	        raise TabulaError("%s needs an argument" % name)
74	    return arg
75	
76	
77	# --- the table -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
78	
79	class Table:
80	    """Column names and rows of strings. `source` names where it came from, for messages."""
81	
82	    def __init__(self, columns, rows, source="<table>"):
83	        self.columns = list(columns)
84	        self.rows = [list(r) for r in rows]
85	        self.source = source
86	
87	    def __len__(self):
88	        return len(self.rows)
89	
90	    def index(self, name):
91	        """Position of a column; TabulaError when there is none."""
92	        try:
93	            return self.columns.index(name)
94	        except ValueError:
95	            raise TabulaError("%s: no column %r (columns: %s)" % (self.source, name, ", ".join(self.columns)))
96	
97	    def column(self, name):
98	        at = self.index(name)
99	        return [row[at] for row in self.rows]
100	
101	    def dicts(self):
102	        return [dict(zip(self.columns, row)) for row in self.rows]
103	
104	    def with_rows(self, rows, columns=None):
105	        return Table(self.columns if columns is None else columns, rows, self.source)
106	
107	
108	def parse_text(text, source):
109	    """CSV text into a Table. Blank lines are ignored; every row must have as many fields as the header."""
110	    if text.startswith("﻿"):
111	        text = text[1:]
112	    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""))
113	    columns, rows = None, []
114	    try:
115	        for fields in reader:
116	            if not fields:
117	                continue
118	            if columns is None:
119	                for name in fields:
120	                    if not name.strip():
121	                        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: empty column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
122	                if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
123	                    raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: duplicate column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
124	                columns = fields
125	                continue
126	            if len(fields) != len(columns):
127	                raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: expected %d fields, found %d"
128	                                  % (source, reader.line_num, len(columns), len(fields)))
129	            rows.append(fields)
130	    except csv.Error as exc:
131	        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: %s" % (source, reader.line_num, exc))
132	    if columns is None:
133	        raise TabulaError("%s: no header line" % source)
134	    return Table(columns, rows, source)
135	
136	
137	def load(path):
138	    """Read a CSV file (UTF-8, optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) into a Table."""
139	    try:
140	        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
141	            raw = fh.read()
142	    except OSError as exc:
143	        raise TabulaError("%s: cannot read: %s" % (path, exc.strerror or exc))
144	    try:
145	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
146	    except UnicodeDecodeError:
147	        raise TabulaError("%s: not valid UTF-8" % path)
148	    return parse_text(text, path)
149

151	# --- output --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
152	
153	def render_text(table):
154	    cells = [table.columns] + table.rows
155	    widths = [max(len(row[i]) for row in cells) for i in range(len(table.columns))]
156	    lines = ["  ".join(cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(row, widths)).rstrip() for row in cells]
157	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
158	
159	
160	def render_csv(table):
161	    out = io.StringIO()
162	    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
163	    writer.writerow(table.columns)
164	    writer.writerows(table.rows)
165	    return out.getvalue()
166	
167	
168	def render_json(table):
169	    return json.dumps(table.dicts(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
170	
171	
172	RENDERERS = {"text": render_text, "csv": render_csv, "json": render_json}
173	
174	
175	def render(table, fmt="text"):
176	    return RENDERERS[fmt](table)
177

"""tabula.engine -- the table model, the transforms, the output formats and the command line.

This is the one module every command lives in. A command is a function `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` that gets the
positional arguments (a list of strings) and the options (a dict) and returns a Table, which `main` then prints in the
format asked for (`--format text|csv|json`, text by default). A mistake in a file or in a request raises TabulaError
(exit status 1); a command line that is not shaped right raises UsageError (exit status 2).
"""
import csv
import io
import json
import re
import sys
import unicodedata
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_DOWN, getcontext

from .errors import TabulaError, UsageError

PROG = "tabula"
FORMATS = ("text", "csv", "json")
getcontext().prec = 60

NUMBER = re.compile(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)")


# --- numbers -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def to_decimal(text):
    """The Decimal a cell holds, or None when it is not a plain decimal number (no exponent, no thousands marks)."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not NUMBER.fullmatch(text):
        return None
    try:
        return Decimal(text)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def fmt_decimal(number):
    """A Decimal as plain text: no exponent, no negative zero."""
    text = format(number, "f")
    if text.startswith("-") and not text.strip("-0."):
        text = text[1:]
    return text


def _need_number(value):
    number = to_decimal(value)
    if number is None:
        raise TabulaError("%r is not a number" % value)
    return number


def _need_count(arg, name):
    if arg is None or not arg.isdigit():
        raise TabulaError("%s needs a whole number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
    return int(arg)


def _need_decimal_arg(arg, name):
    number = None if arg is None else to_decimal(arg)
    if number is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s needs a number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
    return number


def _no_arg(name, arg):
    if arg is not None:
        raise TabulaError("%s takes no argument, got %r" % (name, arg))


def _need_text(arg, name):
    if arg is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s needs an argument" % name)
    return arg


# --- the table -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Table:
    """Column names and rows of strings. `source` names where it came from, for messages."""

    def __init__(self, columns, rows, source="<table>"):
        self.columns = list(columns)
        self.rows = [list(r) for r in rows]
        self.source = source

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.rows)

    def index(self, name):
        """Position of a column; TabulaError when there is none."""
        try:
            return self.columns.index(name)
        except ValueError:
            raise TabulaError("%s: no column %r (columns: %s)" % (self.source, name, ", ".join(self.columns)))

    def column(self, name):
        at = self.index(name)
        return [row[at] for row in self.rows]

    def dicts(self):
        return [dict(zip(self.columns, row)) for row in self.rows]

    def with_rows(self, rows, columns=None):
        return Table(self.columns if columns is None else columns, rows, self.source)


def parse_text(text, source):
    """CSV text into a Table. Blank lines are ignored; every row must have as many fields as the header."""
    if text.startswith("﻿"):
        text = text[1:]
    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""))
    columns, rows = None, []
    try:
        for fields in reader:
            if not fields:
                continue
            if columns is None:
                for name in fields:
                    if not name.strip():
                        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: empty column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
                if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
                    raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: duplicate column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
                columns = fields
                continue
            if len(fields) != len(columns):
                raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: expected %d fields, found %d"
                                  % (source, reader.line_num, len(columns), len(fields)))
            rows.append(fields)
    except csv.Error as exc:
        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: %s" % (source, reader.line_num, exc))
    if columns is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s: no header line" % source)
    return Table(columns, rows, source)


def load(path):
    """Read a CSV file (UTF-8, optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) into a Table."""
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            raw = fh.read()
    except OSError as exc:
        raise TabulaError("%s: cannot read: %s" % (path, exc.strerror or exc))
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        raise TabulaError("%s: not valid UTF-8" % path)
    return parse_text(text, path)


# --- output --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def render_text(table):
    cells = [table.columns] + table.rows
    widths = [max(len(row[i]) for row in cells) for i in range(len(table.columns))]
    lines = ["  ".join(cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(row, widths)).rstrip() for row in cells]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def render_csv(table):
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(table.columns)
    writer.writerows(table.rows)
    return out.getvalue()


def render_json(table):
    return json.dumps(table.dicts(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"


RENDERERS = {"text": render_text, "csv": render_csv, "json": render_json}


def render(table, fmt="text"):
    return RENDERERS[fmt](table)

def parse_spec(spec):
    """`name` or `name:arg` into (function, arg); the argument is everything after the first colon."""
    name, _, arg = spec.partition(":")
    if name not in TRANSFORMS:
        raise TabulaError("unknown transform %r" % name)
    return TRANSFORMS[name], (arg if ":" in spec else None)


def apply_transforms(value, specs):
    for fn, arg in specs:
        value = fn(value, arg)
    return value


# --- commands ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _need_args(args, count, usage):
    if len(args) != count:
        raise UsageError("usage: %s %s" % (PROG, usage))


def cmd_show(args, opts):
    _need_args(args, 1, "show FILE")
    return load(args[0])


def cmd_head(args, opts):
    _need_args(args, 2, "head FILE N")
    if not args[1].isdigit():
        raise UsageError("head: N must be a whole number, got %r" % args[1])
    table = load(args[0])
    return table.with_rows(table.rows[:int(args[1])])


def cmd_cols(args, opts):
    _need_args(args, 1, "cols FILE")
    table = load(args[0])
    return Table(["position", "column"], [[str(i + 1), name] for i, name in enumerate(table.columns)], table.source)


def cmd_apply(args, opts):
    if len(args) < 3:
        raise UsageError("usage: %s apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM..." % PROG)
    table = load(args[0])
    at = table.index(args[1])
    specs = [parse_spec(s) for s in args[2:]]
    rows = []
    for number, row in enumerate(table.rows, 1):
        row = list(row)
        try:
            row[at] = apply_transforms(row[at], specs)
        except TabulaError as exc:
            raise TabulaError("%s: row %d: %s" % (table.source, number, exc))
        rows.append(row)
    return table.with_rows(rows)


COMMANDS = {
    "show": (cmd_show, "show FILE", "print a table"),
    "head": (cmd_head, "head FILE N", "the first N rows"),
    "cols": (cmd_cols, "cols FILE", "the column names, numbered"),
    "apply": (cmd_apply, "apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...", "run transforms over one column"),
}


# --- the command line ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def usage_text():
    lines = ["usage: %s [--format text|csv|json] COMMAND ARGS..." % PROG, "", "commands:"]
    width = max(len(u) for _, u, _ in COMMANDS.values())
    for _, use, what in COMMANDS.values():
        lines.append("  %s  %s" % (use.ljust(width), what))
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def parse_args(argv):
    """(command, positional arguments, options) from the command line."""
    opts, rest, i = {"format": "text"}, [], 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg in ("-h", "--help"):
            opts["help"] = True
        elif arg == "--format" or arg.startswith("--format="):
            if arg == "--format":
                i += 1
                if i >= len(argv):
                    raise UsageError("--format needs a value")
                value = argv[i]
            else:
                value = arg.split("=", 1)[1]
            if value not in FORMATS:
                raise UsageError("--format must be one of %s, got %r" % (", ".join(FORMATS), value))
            opts["format"] = value
        elif arg.startswith("-") and len(arg) > 1:
            raise UsageError("unknown option %s" % arg)
        else:
            rest.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if opts.get("help"):
        return None, rest, opts
    if not rest:
        raise UsageError("no command given")
    if rest[0] not in COMMANDS:
        raise UsageError("unknown command %r" % rest[0])
    return rest[0], rest[1:], opts


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)
    try:
        name, args, opts = parse_args(argv)
        if name is None:
            sys.stdout.write(usage_text())
            return 0
        table = COMMANDS[name][0](args, opts)
        sys.stdout.write(render(table, opts["format"]))
        sys.stdout.flush()
        return 0
    except UsageError as exc:
        print("%s: %s" % (PROG, exc), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    except TabulaError as exc:
        print("%s: %s" % (PROG, exc), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except BrokenPipeError:
        return 0

# Commands

`tabula [--format text|csv|json] COMMAND ARGS...` reads CSV files (UTF-8, an optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) and prints
a table. Every command returns a `Table`; `--format` says how it is printed (text by default). A mistake in a file or in a
request exits 1 with `tabula: <message>` on standard error; a command line that is not shaped right exits 2.

## show

`tabula show FILE` prints the whole table. Blank lines in the file are ignored. A row with more or fewer fields than the
header is a mistake that names the file and the line (`t.csv: line 3: expected 2 fields, found 1`).

## head

`tabula head FILE N` prints the header and the first N rows. N is a whole number (zero is fine); anything else is a usage
error.

## cols

`tabula cols FILE` prints one row per column with two columns, `position` (from 1) and `column`.

## apply

`tabula apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...` runs each TRANSFORM, left to right, over every value of one column and prints the
whole table. A transform is `name` or `name:ARG`; the list is in `docs/transforms.md`. A value a transform cannot take is
a mistake that names the file and the row (`t.csv: row 2: 'abc' is not a number`). Rows count from 1, the header not
counted.

"""The two kinds of failure a command can end in."""


class TabulaError(Exception):
    """A mistake in a file or in what was asked for; the command line ends with exit status 1."""


class UsageError(Exception):
    """A command line that is not shaped right; the command line ends with exit status 2."""

# Commands

`tabula [--format text|csv|json] COMMAND ARGS...` reads CSV files (UTF-8, an optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) and prints
a table. Every command returns a `Table`; `--format` says how it is printed (text by default). A mistake in a file or in a
request exits 1 with `tabula: <message>` on standard error; a command line that is not shaped right exits 2.

## show

`tabula show FILE` prints the whole table. Blank lines in the file are ignored. A row with more or fewer fields than the
header is a mistake that names the file and the line (`t.csv: line 3: expected 2 fields, found 1`).

## head

`tabula head FILE N` prints the header and the first N rows. N is a whole number (zero is fine); anything else is a usage
error.

## cols

`tabula cols FILE` prints one row per column with two columns, `position` (from 1) and `column`.

## apply

`tabula apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...` runs each TRANSFORM, left to right, over every value of one column and prints the
whole table. A transform is `name` or `name:ARG`; the list is in `docs/transforms.md`. A value a transform cannot take is
a mistake that names the file and the row (`t.csv: row 2: 'abc' is not a number`). Rows count from 1, the header not
counted.

## Problem Statement

`tabula` (Python 3.9+, standard library only) has four commands (`show`, `head`, `cols`, `apply`) in `tabula/engine.py`. The user wants seven more table commands — `sort`, `filter`, `group`, `join`, `pivot`, `dedupe`, `stats` — plus two new options, `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`. Everything that works today has to keep working: the four commands, their output, their exit statuses, `pip install .` giving the `tabula` command, and `import tabula`.

## Solution

Each command is a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function in `tabula/engine.py` that returns a `Table`, with one entry in `COMMANDS`. Each also gets its own test file `tests/test_NAME.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats, after the four existing sections and written like them) and a line in the README command list.

Before anything is added, the conventions the module already has become one shared helper each (see Implementation Decisions). Every new command uses those helpers. None of them adds a second way to do the same thing.

## User Stories

1. As a CSV user, I can `tabula sort FILE KEY...` with `:num`/`:desc` modifiers and get a stable multi-key sort.
2. As a CSV user, I can `tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` with `== != >= <= > < ~` and get only the rows where every condition holds.
3. As a CSV user, I can `tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` with `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C`, `mean:C`.
4. As a CSV user, I can `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` with `--kind inner|left`.
5. As a CSV user, I can `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` to sum VALUE into a cross table.
6. As a CSV user, I can `tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` with `--keep first|last`.
7. As a CSV user, I can `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` to get count/min/max/mean/median for each column.

## Implementation Decisions

General rules, from the brief, for every command:
- `--format text|csv|json` (text by default) prints the result table.
- A mistake in a file or in the request prints `tabula: <message>` on stderr, nothing on stdout, and exits 1 (`TabulaError`).
- A command line that is not shaped right exits 2 (`UsageError`): a missing or extra argument, an unknown option, a bad option value, a condition with no operator.
- A column named in a request that the file lacks exits 1, and the message names the column (reuse `Table.index`).
- "row N" counts the file's data rows from 1, header not counted, in file order (never sorted order).
- A **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts. All arithmetic is `Decimal`, never float.
- **Shape checks come before the file is read.** Usage errors (exit 2) are raised before `load`, as `head` does today. Column-existence and cell mistakes (exit 1) come after.

### Shared groundwork: done in issue 1 (`sort`), reused by the other six

"Finish the module's own conventions before adding to them: do not add a second way to do something it already does."
1. **Option reading.** Replace the hard-coded `--format` branch in `parse_args` with one table of choice options, e.g. `OPTIONS = {"format": (FORMATS, "text"), "kind": (("inner", "left"), "inner"), "keep": (("first", "last"), "first")}`, read by one loop that handles both `--opt value` and `--opt=value`. Defaults go into `opts`, so `opts["kind"]` and `opts["keep"]` always exist. Any command line accepts all three options, before or after the command. A bad value is a UsageError, as `--format` is today. The existing `--format` messages stay word for word (`--format needs a value`, `--format must be one of text, csv, json, got 'x'`). Update the usage line in `usage_text()` and the intro of `docs/commands.md` to mention `--kind` and `--keep`.
2. **Argument counts.** Extend `_need_args` so it can also check "at least N" (e.g. `_need_args(args, 2, "sort FILE KEY...", at_least=True)`), and make `cmd_apply` use it, with an unchanged message. Every new command checks its count with `_need_args`.
3. **Row/cell errors.** `cmd_apply` already wraps a cell mistake as `"%s: row %d: %s"`. Make that one helper. On top of it, add a cell-number helper built on `_need_number`/`to_decimal` that raises exactly `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'abc' is not a number`; `%r` is used for both the column and the value, as `_need_number` does. `sort :num`, `group`, `pivot` and `stats` all use this helper. `apply`'s output is unchanged.
4. **Number printing.** Plain numbers (sum/min/max/pivot cells) use the existing `fmt_decimal`, which gives no exponent, no `+` and no negative zero, and keeps `10.50` as `10.50`. Add one helper for "rounded half up to two decimals, always two" (`Decimal("0.01")`, `ROUND_HALF_UP`, then `fmt_decimal`). `group mean`, `stats mean` and `stats median` all use it. A negative zero such as `-0.001` prints `0.00`.
5. **Value comparison.** Add one helper for "compare as numbers when both are numbers, else as text by code point", used by `filter`. `sort :num` uses the cell-number helper; plain `sort` compares text.
6. **Tests.** Move the `run_cli` helper from `tests/test_engine.py` into a shared test-support module (e.g. `tests/support.py`). `test_engine.py` and every new `tests/test_NAME.py` import it from there. Do not copy it.
7. **README.** Turn the README's inline "Commands today: …" sentence into a bulleted command list, one line per command (the four existing ones first). Each command issue then adds its own line in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats.

### Per-command decisions (brief text plus the gaps the brief left open)

**sort** `sort FILE KEY...` (at least one KEY; usage `sort FILE KEY...`)
- A KEY is split on `:`. The first part is the column; each further part must be `num` or `desc`, in either order. A modifier given twice, an unknown modifier, or an empty column part is a usage error.
- Text compares by code point (`B` < `a`). `:num` compares Decimals, and a non-number cell (an empty one included) gives the cell-number error. `:desc` puts the largest first.
- The sort is stable on every key: rows tied on all keys keep file order, also with `:desc`. Use successive stable `sorted` passes from the last key to the first, with `reverse=` for desc. Python's `reverse=True` keeps stability.

**filter** `filter FILE CONDITION...` (at least one)
- Operators: `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `~`. The operator is the one that starts earliest in the argument; where two start at the same place, the longer one wins. The column is the text before it and VALUE the text after it (VALUE may be empty).
- No operator, or nothing before the operator, is a usage error. An unknown column is exit 1.
- For every operator but `~`: if the cell and VALUE are both numbers (`to_decimal`), they are compared as Decimals (`10` > `9`, `1.0` == `1`); otherwise as text by code point.
- `~`: VALUE is contained in the cell, ignoring case, via `.lower()` on both, as `t_icontains` does.
- Rows stay in file order. With no rows left, the header still prints.

**group** `group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` (at least one AGGREGATE)
- An AGGREGATE is `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C` or `mean:C`. Anything else (including `count:x`, `sum:` and an unknown name) is a usage error, and so is the same aggregate twice.
- The output columns are BY, then one per aggregate named with `:` replaced by `_`. If that gives the same column name twice (e.g. BY is `count`), it is a mistake (exit 1) naming the column.
- One row per distinct BY value, in order of first appearance. `count` is the number of rows in the group.
- sum/min/max print with `fmt_decimal` (min/max print the Decimal of the winning cell; among equal values, the first in file order wins). `mean` is the exact sum divided by the count, printed with the 2-decimal helper. Any non-number cell (an empty one included) in an aggregated column gives the cell-number error.

**join** `join LEFT RIGHT KEY` (exactly three)
- KEY must be in both files (exit 1 otherwise, naming the file and the column).
- The result columns are the LEFT columns, then the RIGHT columns except KEY. A RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` appended. If that still leaves a duplicate name, it is a mistake (exit 1).
- A match is exact text equality. `--kind inner` (the default) gives, for each LEFT row in order, one row per matching RIGHT row in RIGHT order. `--kind left` also gives an unmatched LEFT row once, with `""` in the RIGHT columns.

**pivot** `pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` (exactly four)
- ROW == COLUMN is a usage error. VALUE may be the same column as ROW or COLUMN.
- The result columns are ROW, then each distinct COLUMN value in order of first appearance. There is one row per distinct ROW value in order of first appearance.
- A cell is the exact sum of VALUE (printed with `fmt_decimal`); a pair that never occurs is `0`.
- Mistakes are checked row by row in file order:
  - an empty or whitespace-only COLUMN value gives `FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`;
  - a COLUMN value equal to the ROW column's name is a mistake naming the row and the duplicate column;
  - a non-number VALUE gives the cell-number error.

**dedupe** `dedupe FILE KEY...` (at least one)
- Rows with equal text in all the KEY columns form a set. `--keep first` (the default) keeps the first row of each set and `--keep last` keeps the last. The kept rows stay in file order. Repeating a KEY is harmless.

**stats** `stats FILE COLUMN...` (at least one)
- One row per COLUMN, in the order asked (repeats allowed), with the columns `column,count,min,max,mean,median`.
- Only non-empty cells count (`cell.strip() != ""`), and each of them must be a number (cell-number error otherwise).
- min/max print with `fmt_decimal`; mean and median use the 2-decimal helper. The median of an even count is the exact mean of the two middle values.
- A column with no numbers at all gives `COLUMN,0,,,,`.

- Each command has `tests/test_NAME.py` (unittest), driven through the CLI with the shared `run_cli` from the test-support module. Assert the exit status, the exact stdout and the stderr (empty on success; `tabula: …` and empty stdout on failure), across text/csv/json where it matters.

- New dependencies, non-CSV input, changes to transforms or to the existing four commands' behaviour, and float arithmetic.
- Options other than `--kind` and `--keep`.

- [ ] `filter`: all seven operators; earliest operator wins and the longest wins at the same place; numeric comparison when both sides are numbers; `~` case-insensitive; no operator, empty column and no condition exit 2; no rows still prints the header
- [ ] `group`: first-appearance order; `count/sum/min/max/mean` columns named `X_C`; plain-number printing; mean to 2dp half up; a bad or duplicate aggregate and no aggregate exit 2; a non-number exits 1; a duplicate output column exits 1

- [ ] `dedupe`: `--keep first|last`; kept rows in file order; no KEY exits 2
- [ ] `stats`: `column,count,min,max,mean,median`; blank cells skipped; exact median; 2dp mean/median; `COLUMN,0,,,,` when there are no numbers; no COLUMN exits 2

## What to build

Implement PRD #1 in full. Its body is the contract; the acceptance criteria below are copied from it word for word.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parse_args` reads `--format`, `--kind`, `--keep` from one option table; `--kind`/`--keep` are accepted on any command line, before or after the command, as `--opt v` or `--opt=v`; a bad value exits 2; `--format` messages are unchanged
- [ ] One "at least N arguments" check (`_need_args`), one row-error helper, one cell-number helper (`FILE: row N: column 'C': 'x' is not a number`), one 2-decimal formatter; `apply` uses the shared helpers with unchanged output
- [ ] `run_cli` lives in one shared test-support module, used by `test_engine.py` and every new test file
- [ ] `sort`: multi-key, `:num`/`:desc` in either order, code-point text order, stable (also with `:desc`); a duplicate or unknown modifier and no KEY exit 2; a non-number with `:num` exits 1 with the exact message
- [ ] `filter`: all seven operators; earliest operator wins and the longest wins at the same place; numeric comparison when both sides are numbers; `~` case-insensitive; no operator, empty column and no condition exit 2; no rows still prints the header
- [ ] `group`: first-appearance order; `count/sum/min/max/mean` columns named `X_C`; plain-number printing; mean to 2dp half up; a bad or duplicate aggregate and no aggregate exit 2; a non-number exits 1; a duplicate output column exits 1
- [ ] `join`: LEFT columns then RIGHT minus KEY; `_right` renaming; a remaining duplicate exits 1; inner/left semantics and ordering; not exactly 3 args exits 2
- [ ] `pivot`: column/row order by first appearance; exact sums; missing pairs are `0`; ROW==COLUMN exits 2; an empty COLUMN value, a COLUMN value equal to the ROW name and a non-number VALUE exit 1; not exactly 4 args exits 2
- [ ] `dedupe`: `--keep first|last`; kept rows in file order; no KEY exits 2
- [ ] `stats`: `column,count,min,max,mean,median`; blank cells skipped; exact median; 2dp mean/median; `COLUMN,0,,,,` when there are no numbers; no COLUMN exits 2
- [ ] Each command has a `COMMANDS` entry, `tests/test_NAME.py`, a `docs/commands.md` section (order: sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats) and a README list line
- [ ] The four existing commands, their output and exit statuses, `pip install .` → `tabula`, and `import tabula` still work; the full test suite passes

None

#1

**sort** `sort FILE KEY...` (at least one KEY; usage `sort FILE KEY...`)
- A KEY is split on `:`. The first part is the column; each further part must be `num` or `desc`, in either order. A modifier given twice, an unknown modifier, or an empty column part is a usage error.

This issue also lands the **shared groundwork** every other command reuses:

#### Shared groundwork: done in issue 1 (`sort`), reused by the other six

"Finish the module's own conventions before adding to them: do not add a second way to do something it already does."

Defaults go into `opts`, so `opts["kind"]` and `opts["keep"]` always exist. Any command line accepts all three options, before or after the command. The fleet is running and has started the first command, `sort` (#3). The other six will follow one at a time, since the pool size is 1.

**Board** (VocanicZ/bench-20261118-long-default-harness-r01):
- **#1** is the plan (PRD). It holds the rules for each command, the gaps I decided myself, the acceptance criteria, and your request word for word as the top authority.
- **#3 `sort`** also carries the shared groundwork, because the brief says to finish the module's own conventions first. It makes one of each:
  - a single option table for `--format`, `--kind` and `--keep`;
  - one argument-count check (`_need_args` with an "at least" form);
  - one helper for the `FILE: row N: column 'C': … is not a number` message;
  - one formatter for two-decimal output.

  It also moves the tests' `run_cli` into one shared test module and turns the README command list into one line per command.
- **#4–#9** are filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe and stats. Each waits only on #3, not on each other.

**One correction I made:** at a pool size of 1, the engine skipped splitting the plan and filed one issue for everything (#2). That went against your "seven issues, one per command", so I stopped the pool and closed #2. The lane had made no commits, so nothing was lost. I then filed the seven issues by hand in the engine's format and restarted.

**Decisions I made where the brief was silent:**
- Usage errors (exit 2) are checked before the file is read.
- An unknown `sort` modifier is a usage error.
- An empty cell counts as "not a number" in `sort :num`, `group` and `pivot`; only `stats` skips empty cells.
- A `group` result that would have the same column name twice exits 1.
- A whitespace-only COLUMN value in `pivot` counts as empty.
- `~` ignores case the same way the existing `icontains` transform does.

The engine's estimate was about 92 minutes and $14.50 for the fleet, against about 7 minutes and $1.29 done directly. Weekly usage on this account was at 62% when the run started; the fleet checkpoints its work at 90%. `.harness/` is untracked in the repo and I did not commit it.

**Where to watch:** `harness status --watch` for the live dashboard (Ctrl-C stops watching, not the fleet), `harness web` at http://127.0.0.1:4637/, or `/harness-status`.
